seo.meta_title: What Does 눈칫밥 먹다 Mean? | Korean Food Idiom AI Gets Wrong
seo.meta_description: AI translates 눈칫밥 먹다 as 'eat nunchi rice'. It means living or working where you feel unwelcome and must watch everyone's mood.

ai_failure.situation: A Korean friend who just started a new job sighs: 요즘 회사에서 눈칫밥 먹고 있어.
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Translates it as 'I'm eating nunchi rice at work' or 'eating food with good sense'.
ai_failure.why_it_fails: 눈치 is reading other people's moods. 눈칫밥 is the meal you eat while worrying how others see you — at a relative's house you depend on, in a new team, under in-laws. It means feeling like a burden and tiptoeing around everyone.

natural_solution.rule: 눈칫밥(을) 먹다 = live or work somewhere you feel unwelcome, constantly watching others' moods. Spelled 눈칫밥, though many people write 눈치밥.

alternatives.context: 'I'm new, so I'm tiptoeing around everyone' — self-deprecating, common at work

alternatives.phrase: 어릴 때 친척 집에서 눈칫밥 먹으면서 컸어요.
alternatives.romanization: eo-ril ttae chin-cheok ji-be-seo nun-chit-bap meo-geu-myeon-seo keo-sseo-yo
alternatives.context: 'I grew up at relatives' houses, always feeling like a burden' — serious, emotional
Everyday, lighter version: 'I feel awkward / I feel like I should be careful here'

nuance: Korean measures belonging through food. Being fed freely means you're family; eating while someone watches the rice pot means you're a guest who's overstayed. That's why 눈칫밥 carries so much weight: it describes a whole childhood or a whole first year at a job in one word. If a Korean says it about their past, respond with sympathy (많이 힘드셨겠어요), not a food joke.
